items.title: Bondi terror attack survivor received 'influx of hate' hours after shooting
items.description: Deepfake and altered images depicting a Bondi Beach terror attack survivor holding an Academy Award while covered in blood spread "like wildfire" online just hours after the shooting, a royal commission has heard.

items.title: Victorian MP says she misunderstood meaning of 'headlock' in assault allegation
items.description: State Liberal MP Moira Deeming says she misunderstood the meaning of the term "headlock", after alleging her party room colleague Matthew Guy assaulted her.

items.title: Super switching sees billions flow out of traditional funds, at a risk
items.description: There is now more than $1 trillion in self-managed superannuation funds, which means a big chunk of money isn't regulated by APRA, and it's the rate of the shift into SMSFs and less-regulated managed investment schemes that has regulators worried.

items.title: Live: 'It's time': Liberal frontbencher calls for party to rebrand
items.description: Liberal frontbencher Melissa McIntosh says her party needs a rebrand after support for the Coalition hit a new low in the latest opinion polls. Follow live.

items.title: Vanuatu critical infrastructure to remain 'free from militarisation' under pact
items.description: Vanuatu's Prime Minister Jotham Napat and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese ink the Nakamal Agreement, almost 10 months after Mr Napat pulled out of a planned signing ceremony in Port Vila, citing concerns around sovereignty.

items.title: 'I've got all the symptoms': Matty Robbins was a hero of the AFL. Now he's suffering
items.description: More than 30 professional and amateur Aussie Rules players have been diagnosed with CTE, revealing that the brain trauma crisis is striking all levels of the game.

items.title: Allan government under pressure amid latest Big Build corruption allegations
items.description: The Victorian premier has backed her government's response to corruption in the construction industry, despite criticism from across politics and integrity experts.

items.title: Health minister stops short of requesting coronial inquest into baby's death
items.description: WA's health minister says she would support a coronial inquest into the death of an eight-month-old girl at Kalgoorlie Health Campus, but says it is a decision for the state coroner.

items.title: France records 1,000 excess daily deaths as record heatwave broken by severe storms
items.description: More than 150 million Europeans swelter in "extreme heat", which scientists say has been the worst the continent has ever recorded.

items.title: Family who spent $250,000 on IVF welcomes new rebate scheme in SA
items.description: A South Australian couple who spent $250,000 on fertility treatments say the government's IVF rebate will make a "huge difference" for people trying to conceive.

items.title: Broncos winger Josiah Karapani dropped from team after alleged drink driving
items.description: In a statement, the club confirmed the 24-year-old had been issued with a notice to appear in court and would not be available for the next NRL game.

items.title: Expanded World Cup called 'vulgar and ordinary' by Ghana coach. Is that fair?
items.description: Ghana's coach Carlos Queiroz has lashed out at FIFA's expanded 48-team World Cup, despite his team progressing. Is his criticism justified as the tournament moves into the knockout stage?

items.title: Ben Stokes's retirement a perfect example of his main character energy
items.description: Ben Stokes has been the centre of England's cricketing universe for 15 years. In announcing his retirement mid-match, he highlighted how damaging that main character energy can be.

items.title: Les Mills, NZ Olympian and founder of global fitness brand, dies aged 91
items.description: The New Zealand Olympian who opened an Auckland gym in 1968 that grew into an international group fitness brand has died aged 91.

items.title: Quick and easy dinners using inexpensive chickpeas
items.description: From comforting curry to hearty soup, these easy recipes will get chickpeas out of the pantry and onto the menu.

items.title: Outback town set to star in new thriller as film festival kicks off
items.description: Red Dog director Kriv Stenders reveals plans for a new thriller film as the annual Vision Splendid Outback Film Festival kicks off in Winton.

items.title: History quiz: Test your knowledge from this decade to the 1600s
items.description: This week was a big one in times gone by. From this decade to the 17th century, put your history knowledge to the test.

items.title: NASA to bump telescope back into space to avoid it falling to Earth
items.description: US space agency NASA is racing to save an aging telescope, used to observe cosmic explosions, from falling back to Earth with a daring rescue mission.

items.title: US and Iran to halt strikes as talks set to continue
items.description: The US and Iran will stand down on strikes and vessels will be allowed to move freely, as technical talks are slated to continue on all areas of the memorandum of understanding.

items.title: Live: Renewed Gulf hostilities put markets on edge, ASX inches up
items.description: Local stocks begin the week higher as the end of financial year approaches. Wall Street was weighed down by another bout of selling in the tech sector. Follow market updates plus business news and analysis at our live blog.

items.title: The Gulf will 'not go back to where it was' after the Iran war
items.description: Before a flare-up in fighting over the weekend, the interim deal between the United States and Iran was giving the region something it badly needs, analysts say.

items.title: Last week was a turning point inside the Liberal party
items.description: While Angus Taylor grapples with the Coalition's dilemma of how to keep the centre while diverting voters away from Pauline Hanson's party, Andrew Hastie has been talking tough on One Nation.

items.title: Baby, young boys pulled alive from Venezuela earthquake rubble
items.description: The three children are among at least 33 people rescued during a weekend multinational operation that continued searching for survivors, while thousands remained unaccounted-for.

items.title: Crisafulli confirms children in state care have slept in government offices
items.description: David Crisafulli was briefed after the Together Union acknowledged over the weekend it was aware of reports of children sleeping in child safety offices.

items.title: Williams takes aim at anti-doping measures ahead of Wimbledon return
items.description: As she prepares for her All England Club comeback, Serena Williams claims the tennis anti-doping protocol is "unprofessional" and "unreasonable".
